about: Load budgets for the console shell (index.html) produced by `npm run build:web`. Sizes are gzip bytes of the emitted files, measured from dist-web/.vite/manifest.json so the initial-load set is the real static dependency graph, not a guess. Run `node scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs --update-baseline` after an intentional size change and explain the move in the pull request.

measurement.compression: node:zlib gzipSync, default level (matches the sizes Vite prints)
measurement.baselineToolchain: vite 5.4.21 production build, Node 22, linux x64

notes: Initial load = the entry chunk plus every chunk it imports statically, plus the entry CSS and the HTML document. Everything else (home scene, each game, Model Studio, three/Rapier, nipplejs) is fetched on demand.
The engine vendor chunk (three + Rapier + Renderoni core, ~900 kB gzip) must stay out of the initial graph. maxInitialChunkRawBytes is the tripwire for that.
Frame rate is not measured here. 45 FPS on mid/high phones is a product target that is checked by hand on real devices; see docs/beta-release-checklist.md.
Limits are deliberately above the baseline so ordinary work does not fail CI, while tolerancePercent still fails a meaningful regression. Lower maxBytes as the shell gets smaller.

mustStayLazy.why: Touch sticks are loaded only after a real touch, so desktop and keyboard users never download nipplejs.

budgets.label: Initial console shell JS (entry + static imports, gzip)
Total initial load: HTML + shell JS + CSS (gzip)
Largest lazy chunk, currently three + Rapier + engine (gzip)
